messages:
ashley (support): Jordan opened a ticket: customer gets 403s from our hosted API after migrating a subset of subnets to use a VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink). They say it only happens from one AZ/subnet. Can you share minimal repro and any DNS/route info?
customer-jordan: repro steps i used:
  - from app host in subnet-09 run: `curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health`
  - result: TLS handshake OK, then HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
  - from same instance `dig api.redwood.ai +short` returns `vpce-abc123-012345.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com.` sometimes, sometimes the public CNAME
  - attaching snips: `curl -v` shows `Server: redwood` and `x-request-id: r-zzzz`
ashley (support): thanks. two quick checks: 1) is Private DNS enabled on the VPCE? 2) what's the VPC endpoint policy? sometimes policy or missing route assoc causes traffic to hit the wrong backend.
matt (infra): also check route table assoc for that subnet — endpoint needs a route/table target for the service prefix list or interface ENIs; if the subnet isn't associated you'll hairpin to internet NAT instead. can you paste the route table entries?
customer-jordan: route table excerpt:
  rtb-0a: 10.0.0.0/16 local
  0.0.0.0/0 igw-0b
  (no route to vpce or prefix list)
  security group outbound: 0.0.0.0/0: TCP 443 ALLOW
  NACL: 100 ALLOW ALL, 110 DENY 32768-65535 TCP (we use a strict ephemeral rule)
kevin (sre): ah — that NACL DENY for ephemeral ports is a likely culprit. Interface endpoints use ephemeral source ports on the client side; asymmetric blocking can break TLS handshakes or cause backend to see unexpected source. Also if DNS sometimes resolves public CNAME, traffic will go out via IGW and hit our public LB which rejects or returns 403 for that origin/account combo.
ashley (support): quick test: on the instance `dig +short api.redwood.ai` then `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:10.10.5.8 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` where 10.10.5.8 is the vpce ENI IP. That confirms whether the endpoint IP answers OK with the same Host header.
customer-jordan: ran that. with `--resolve` to the ENI IP I still got 403. output snippet: `* Connected to api.redwood.ai (10.10.5.8) port 443 (#0)\n* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Finished\n< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\n< x-amzn-RequestId: abc-123`.
matt (infra): 403 from the endpoint itself suggests endpoint policy or service-side permission check (resource-based policy on the service / API Gateway authorizer) rather than routing. Can you paste the VPC endpoint policy JSON?
customer-jordan: policy currently: `{ "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::777777777777:role/svc-role" }, "Action": "execute-api:Invoke", "Resource": "*" } ] }` — we locked it to a specific role during test.
kevin (sre): there it is. because traffic originates from the customer's VPC and our service evaluates principal or source VPC, restricting to that role will cause requests from normal app instances to be rejected with 403. For VPC endpoints we often need either a permissive policy for the service with condition on aws:sourceVpce or explicitly allow the calling account principals.
ashley (support): recommended minimal fix: update VPCE policy to allow `Principal: "*"` with `Condition: { "StringEquals": { "aws:sourceVpce": "vpce-abcdef" } }` or add the customers' account principals. Also make sure Private DNS is enabled if you expect `api.redwood.ai` to resolve to the VPCE.
customer-jordan: updated policy to allow sourceVpce condition and re-tested — now `curl` returns 200 OK for the `--resolve` test and normal `dig` returns the vpce CNAME consistently.
kevin (sre): follow-up: remove that NACL DENY on ephemeral ports (or add explicit allow entries for 1024-65535) so responses from endpoints don't get blocked. Also confirm security group on the endpoint ENIs allows inbound from the client subnet ephemeral range if you have SG restrictions.
ashley (support): to summarize action items for the ticket: 1) enable Private DNS on VPCE if needed, 2) adjust endpoint policy to allow callers (sourceVpce condition recommended), 3) associate route table / ensure subnet is using endpoint & not routing via IGW, 4) allow ephemeral port range in NACLs and SGs, 5) if using a NAT instance, disable source/dest check or prefer managed NAT Gateway. I'll mark this as resolved from support side but keep ticket open for docs updates.
customer-jordan: thanks all — will update infra ASG preflight to include ephemeral allow and add a policy template to our IaC. saved our go-live.
deploy-bot: Deployment notice: rollout to us-west-2 finished (canary 5% -> 100%). PR #8421 referenced in ticket.
ashley (support): nice, closing loop. I'll add a short KB entry with the policy snippet and the `curl --resolve` repro. :thumbsup:
